questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: assign oxygen its usual oxidation number in a binary compound
questions.stem: A student assigns oxidation numbers in a water molecule. What value does the oxygen carry there?

options.misconception: borrows the peroxide value for an ordinary oxide
gives oxygen the value hydrogen usually carries
treats any oxygen as if it were elemental oxygen gas

questions.explanation: Oxygen is more electronegative than hydrogen, so both O-H bonds push the shared electrons onto oxygen, giving it -1 per bond and -2 in total. The -1 value applies to oxygen in peroxides such as H2O2, where an O-O bond splits the electrons evenly, and 0 applies only to free elemental oxygen.
questions.hint: Assign the shared electrons to the more electronegative atom.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: solve for nitrogen in ammonium chloride using the sum-to-zero rule
questions.stem: What is the oxidation number of the nitrogen atom in ammonium chloride, NH4Cl?

options.misconception: drops the sign when solving the sum equation
borrows the chloride value and applies it to nitrogen
uses nitrogen's value in the nitrate ion here

questions.explanation: NH4Cl is neutral, so the values must sum to zero. Taking chloride as -1 gives nitrogen + 4(+1) = +1, hence nitrogen = 1 - 4 = -3. Reading the +1 charge of the ammonium ion as nitrogen's own value is the classic slip; the sum rule, not the ion name, sets the number.
questions.hint: Subtract the hydrogens' total from the ion's total charge.

questions.stem: What oxidation number is assigned to each chlorine atom in liquid Cl2 at 25 degrees Celsius?

options.misconception: imports the chloride value into the neutral element

options.text: Plus one, as chlorine shows with a partner atom

options.misconception: borrows an oxyanion value for a diatomic element

questions.explanation: An element in its own elemental form has oxidation number zero because identical atoms divide the bonding electrons equally, so each chlorine in Cl2 is 0. questions.stem: In the reaction CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O, which element undergoes oxidation?

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: select the balanced equation for a redox reaction in acid
questions.stem: Which equation correctly balances the reaction of dichromate with iodide in acidic solution?

options.misconception: halves the hydrogen and water needed to match seven oxygens
doubles the chromium so the equation no longer balances atoms
uses three iodides, giving only half the needed electrons

questions.explanation: The reduction half is Cr2O7(2-) + 14H+ + 6e- -> 2Cr(3+) + 7H2O, with charge -2 + 14 - 6 = +6 on each side, and the oxidation half is 6I- -> 3I2 + 6e-, matching those six electrons. Charges (-2 - 6 + 14 = +6) and atoms (2 Cr, 7 O, 14 H, 6 I) then balance, which the other coefficients fail.

questions.learningObjective: apply the charge-conservation test to a half-reaction
questions.stem: Beyond matching atom counts, what must every balanced half-reaction also satisfy?

The charge difference must equal the electrons shown
